description:
Independent developer specializing in low-level engineering and software development (C++, Assembly).

Focused on building an autonomous system for telemetry processing and biometric health monitoring designed for long-duration deep-space missions. Equipped with strong backend, algorithm design, and data processing skills, with a keen interest in embedded and hardware systems.
summary:
Aegis-Bio is an interactive astronaut health monitoring application designed for long-duration space missions (ISS, Moon bases, and Mars transit) where Earth communication delays prevent real-time medical supervision.

Based on NASA Human Research Program (HRP) guidelines and Canadian Space Agency (CSA) space radiation research, the app tracks 7 core indicators: heart rate, blood pressure, blood sugar (mg/dL), body temperature, sleep hours, mood, and daily space radiation dose (mSv/day).

Crew members can switch between four mission environments (ISS Space Station, Flight to Mars, Moon Base, Space Rover), click on an interactive human body figure to inspect specific organ risks, log daily readings onto a trend chart, and follow clear Green/Yellow/Red action steps and daily workout/hydration checklists. A companion C++17 console module implements the same health threshold logic for lightweight onboard evaluation.
details:
Links & Overview

Live Web App: https://aegis-bio.netlify.app

Interactive Simulator (also available in web app): https://aegis-bio.netlify.app/simulation.html

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/8080gate/aegis-bio

7-Slide Presentation: https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1wu1xfXXPGAtKfBZuK1jEC_s3guYIUCuK/edit?usp=sharing

Aegis-Bio is an autonomous astronaut health monitor built by Ursulyak Ion (@dursulyak) and Kika Ivan (@fanat225) for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge.

On a Mars flight, one-way radio delay reaches 18 to 20 minutes, so crews cannot wait up to 40 minutes for mission control on Earth to answer a medical question. Aegis-Bio converts raw vitals and radiation readings into instant color-coded risk triage and plain-language actions onboard.

What Aegis-Bio Does & How It Works

The web flight console integrates three panels:

  1. Anatomical X-Ray Map: Astronauts click four body zones (Head & Brain, Ribcage & Heart, Kidneys & Metabolism, Skeleton & Radiation Shield). Each region highlights in Green, Yellow, or Red and explains spaceflight effects on that organ system.
  2. Live Telemetry & Simulator Controls: Users adjust seven metrics via sliders or quick scenarios (Normal, Tired / Low Sleep, High Radiation, High Sugar / Stress): Heart Rate (52-95 bpm), Blood Pressure (<135/88 mmHg), Blood Sugar (70-125 mg/dL), Body Temperature (36.0-37.4 C), Sleep (>=6.5 hours), Mood (6-10), and Space Radiation (<1.0 mSv/day, CSA CANS model). A live Canvas ECG traces the real pulse rate, and "Log Check (+)" appends points to a 10-check trend graph.
  3. Autonomous Triage & Daily Checklist: Any threshold alert updates the status badge and generates immediate steps (drink 500 ml of water, get 7.5 hours of sleep, skip sugary snacks, or move to a shielded module). A 4-item daily checklist reinforces strength exercise and hydration.

A companion C++17 module (`include/health_monitor.hpp`, `src/main.cpp`) mirrors the same threshold logic for lightweight onboard CLI execution.

Key Benefits

  • Zero-delay medical triage usable without specialized clinical training.
  • Mission-aware thresholds across four profiles: ISS Space Station (0.2s delay), Moon Base (1.3s), Space Rover (1.3s), and Flight to Mars (18 min).
  • Bilingual crew interface switching instantly between English and Ukrainian (EN / UA).

Intended Impact

As Artemis lunar habitats and Mars transit missions reduce Earth dependency, early self-checks prevent minor dehydration, sleep loss, glucose spikes, or solar storm radiation exposure from escalating into emergencies. Aegis-Bio supports crew autonomy in deep space and analog research stations on Earth.

How Our Project Is Creative

Rather than burying crew members in raw spreadsheets, Aegis-Bio pairs an interactive anatomical X-ray skeleton with a real-time ECG trace and Earth-delay indicator. Clicking any body zone turns complex biomedical numbers into one clear action plan.

Factors Our Team Considered (NASA HRP & CSA Science)

Thresholds and clinical notes reflect five NASA HRP spaceflight hazards (radiation, altered gravity, isolation, distance from Earth, and closed habitats) alongside Canadian Space Agency (CSA) research:

  • Microgravity fluid shift raises cranial pressure behind the eyes while deconditioning the heart.
  • CSA ISS studies link weightlessness to insulin resistance (tracked via blood sugar in mg/dL) and ~1% monthly bone loss without daily exercise.
  • CSA CANS research notes ~30% of spacecraft dose comes from secondary neutrons off hull walls, driving stricter limits inside rovers and deep-space transit.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

  • Web Application: HTML5, CSS3, Vanilla JavaScript, Interactive SVG Anatomy, HTML5 Canvas
  • Core Evaluator: C++17 with CMake
  • Hosting: Netlify (web deployment), GitHub (MIT repository)
